title: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: Sums of two squares, Landherr's theorem and the Hasse principle for unitary cocycles
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.note:
Let `E` be a CM field with `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E`, and let `F` be its maximal real subfield.
The file starts with a result on sums of two squares in quadratic algebras over `F`. It then proves
Landherr's theorem: a hermitian space that has an orthonormal frame at the finite places is
determined up to rational isometry by its signs at the infinite places. Finally it proves the Hasse
principle for cocycles of a cyclic Galois group of prime order in the definite unitary group, which
is used for base change. There `E' / E` is a Galois extension of CM fields of prime degree, and
`σ ≠ 1` generates its group.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_sq_add_sq_quadraticAlgebra`: for `E` with a CM type, a totally positive `p` in `F` is
  a sum of two squares in `F[X] / (X² - (q p - B²))` for every `B` in `F`. This holds when `p` has
  valuation `1` outside a set `S` of finite places of `E`, and `q` has valuation `1` at the places
  of `S` and at their complex conjugates.
* `New.Core.exists_form_eq_one`: a hermitian matrix representing `1` over the adeles does so over
  `E`.
* `New.Core.exists_rat_frame_of_adelic`: the same for a diagonal matrix of signs, by induction on
  the columns.
* `New.Space.landherr`, `New.Space.exists_x_eq_and_ratEmbed_conj_eq`: two spaces with the same signs
  differ by a rational change of basis and by moving the point.
* `New.U.hasse_principle_coboundary`: a cocycle that splits over the finite adeles splits
  rationally; the proof combines Hilbert 90 for `GL n` with Landherr's theorem `New.Space.landherr`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CMType`: makes the field `E` a CM number field with a chosen complex embedding `Φ w` of `E`
  for each infinite place `w`.
* `New.𝔸`: the product of one copy of `ℂ` for each infinite place of `E` and the finite adeles
  `𝔸f E`; this is the adele ring of `E` when `E` is totally complex.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point. It is a matrix `J` over `E` and `x : GL n (𝔸 E)`
  with `xᴴ J x` equal to `New.stdForm E s`, which is `diag(s)` at the infinite places and `1` at
  the finite places.
modules.literature:
Known result: Landherr's Hasse principle for hermitian forms. The Hasse principle is proved only
for adelically unimodular spaces of equal signature over a CM field containing the roots of unity of
order 5040. It uses Hasse's norm theorem and strong approximation for the adeles instead of
Hasse-Minkowski. Source: W.
Landherr, Äquivalenz Hermitescher Formen über einem beliebigen algebraischen Zahlkörper, Abh. Math.
Sem. Hamburg 11 (1936) 245-248; M. Kneser, Lectures on Galois cohomology of classical groups, TIFR
47 (1969), §5.5.

modules.title: Finite adeles of number fields: topology, idempotents, functoriality and base change
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adeles of number fields, characters and approximation
modules.note:
This file develops the finite adeles `New.𝔸f E` of a number field `E` and their subring `New.Ô E` of
integral adeles. The valuation `Valued.v` of a completion, written `v`, is multiplicative with
values in `ℤᵐ⁰` (the integers, written multiplicatively by `exp`, with a zero adjoined), so that
integral elements have `v ≤ 1`. The file covers the topology of completions and finite adeles, and
the idempotents `New.idem` of sets of places. It also covers functoriality along embeddings of
number fields through `New.adeleMap`, and base change along an extension `L / K`. For CM fields,
complex conjugation `star` is extended to places and finite adeles, and commutes with
`New.adeleMap`; it induces maps `New.conjLoc` between the completions at conjugate places.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.FinPlace`, `New.LocField`, `New.LocInt`, `New.ResField`: finite places, completions, their
  integers and residue fields; `New.𝔸f`, `New.Ô`: finite adeles and integral finite adeles;
  `New.evalAt w` is the ring homomorphism taking a finite adele to its component in the completion
  `New.LocField w`.
* `New.isCompact_Ô`, `New.isOpen_Ô`: the integral adeles `New.Ô E` are compact and open.
* `New.denseRange_algebraMap_Ô`, `New.denseRange_algebraMap_finAdele`: `𝓞 E` is dense in `Ô E` and
  `E` is dense in the finite adeles (strong approximation), which are a Polish space.
* `New.adeleCombination`: for a basis `b` of `L / K`, the map `(a i) ↦ ∑ a i • b i` from `ι → 𝔸f K`
  to `𝔸f L`.
* `New.isHomeomorph_adeleCombination`: this map is a homeomorphism.
* `New.mem_range_finAdeleIncl_iff`: for `L / K` Galois, the adeles fixed by `Gal(L/K)` are those
  from `K`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the topology of the finite adeles of a number field, strong approximation and base
change. Base change is proved for finite adeles only, and the full adeles are those of totally
complex fields with chosen embeddings.

Source: J. W. S. Cassels, Global Fields, in Cassels-Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory, 1967, ch. II
§§14-16; A. Weil, Basic Number Theory, ch. IV.

modules.title: The additive character, Haar measures and the rational lattice in the adeles
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adeles of number fields, characters and approximation
modules.note:
The adeles `New.𝔸` of a number field `E` are one copy of `ℂ` for each infinite place, times the
finite adeles `New.𝔸f`; this is the adele ring when `E` is totally complex. `New.Ô` is the ring of
integral finite adeles. The file defines the standard additive character and the Haar measures
used in Fourier analysis on `New.𝔸`. For a totally complex field `E`, it proves that `E`, embedded
diagonally by `New.toAdele`, is a cocompact lattice of covolume one, and so are vectors and matrices
over `E`. The proof uses a fundamental domain built from a fractional ideal.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ψf`: the character of the finite adeles that is trivial on `New.Ô` (`New.ψf_eq_one_of_mem`)
  and is `𝐞 (tr a)` on `a ∈ E` (`New.ψf_coe`), where `𝐞 t = exp (2πi t)`. These two properties
  define it, since every finite adele is an element of `E` plus an integral one.
* `New.stdAddChar`: its product with `𝐞 (-∑_w 2 re x_w)`. Here `x_w` is the component of the adele
  at the infinite place `w`.
* `New.volume_Ô`: `volume` on the finite adeles gives `New.Ô` the mass `New.volÔ`. On a completion
  `New.LocField w`, `volume` gives the local integers mass one (`New.volume_LocInt`). On the adeles
  it is the product with Lebesgue measure on each `ℂ`.
* `New.ratAdeles`, `New.ratVectors`, `New.ratMatrices`: the rational points, vectors and matrices.
* `New.HasFundDomain`: a compact set contains a fundamental domain of volume one.
* `New.IsCovolOneLattice`: a discrete cocompact subgroup whose quotient measure has mass one.

Notions from other files:
* `New.LocField`, `New.LocInt`: The completion E_w of E at the finite place w and its ring of
  integers.
* `New.PlaceEmbedding E`: a choice, for each infinite place `w`, of a complex embedding `Φ w` of
  `E` that induces `w`. The map `New.toAdele` uses these embeddings at the infinite places.
modules.literature:
For totally complex `E` the file proves a known result: a number field is a discrete subgroup of its
adeles with compact quotient, here with a measure for which the covolume is one.

modules.title: Standard character, self-duality, strong approximation and one-sided Poisson summation
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adeles of number fields, characters and approximation
modules.note:
Let `E` be a totally complex field with adele ring `New.𝔸 E`, and let `New.toAdele` be the diagonal
embedding of `E`. `New.stdAddChar` is the standard additive character, and its finite part `New.ψf`
is trivial on the integral adeles `New.Ô`. The file shows that, over a CM field, rational points of
unitary groups are discrete in the adelic group. It treats the conductor and nondegeneracy of the
character, proves that `E` is its own annihilator (also for matrices), and proves strong
approximation for adeles and adelic matrices. It ends with a one-sided Poisson summation inequality
and the compact open group given by the inverse different among self-adjoint finite adeles.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.discreteTopology_Gamma`: `New.Space.Γ` is discrete, because the rational matrices
  `New.ratMatrices` are discrete among the adelic ones. So the image under `New.Space.ratEmbed` of
  any subgroup is discrete.
* `New.stdAddChar_toAdele`, `New.mem_ratAdeles_of_stdAddChar_eq_one`: for `E` totally complex,
  `New.stdAddChar` is trivial on `E`. An adele that pairs trivially with all of `E` lies in `E`. So
  `E` is its own annihilator.
* `New.isDualFamily_ratAdeles`: the characters `x ↦ stdAddChar E (toAdele a * x)`, `a : E`, form a
  dual family for the adeles modulo `E`.
* `New.isDualFamily_ratMatrices`: the same for matrices, with the trace pairing.
* `New.strong_approximation`: strong approximation; `E` plus the adeles supported on a nonempty set
  `S` of finite places is dense in the adeles.
* `New.Exchange.denseRange_rat_matrix_add`: strong approximation for matrices.

Notions from other files:
* `New.𝔸f E`, `New.Ô E`: the finite adeles of `E` and the subring of integral finite adeles.
* `New.PlaceEmbedding.Φ`: a chosen complex embedding `Φ w` of `E` for each infinite place `w`; the
  adele ring `New.𝔸 E` is the product of one copy of `ℂ` for each `w` with `New.𝔸f E`.
* `New.ratAdeles`, `New.ratMatrices`: the images of `E` and of the matrices over `E` under
  `New.toAdele`, as additive subgroups.
* `New.IsDualFamily B₀ χ`: `i ↦ χ i` is an injective homomorphism to the continuous unitary
  characters trivial on `B₀`, and the common kernel of the `χ i` lies in `B₀`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Self-duality of a number field in its adeles, strong approximation and a Poisson
inequality. For totally complex fields only, the field is shown to be its own annihilator and the
pairing is shown to be non-degenerate. Strong approximation omits a nonempty set of finite places
and is deduced from duality. Poisson summation is proved only as an inequality, for nonnegative
integrable functions that are lower semicontinuous at the rational points of the sum. Source: J.
Tate, Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions, thesis 1950, in Cassels-Fröhlich
ch. XV, Theorem 4.1.4; for strong approximation, Cassels, ch. II §15.

See also `Lib.Adelic.Unitary.WeakApproximation`.

modules.title: The module of an idele, Haar measure scaling and the norm map on finite adeles
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adeles of number fields, characters and approximation
modules.note:
This file studies the module of an idele of a number field `E`, its relation to Haar measure, and
its behaviour under norms. Here `New.𝔸 E` has one copy of `ℂ` for each infinite place. The module
`New.ideleAbs` is therefore the product of the squared norms at the infinite places and of the norms
at the finite places. The generalised index `New.genIndex a` of a finite idele, defined through the
scaling of Haar measure, is the inverse of its module; it is `[Ô : a Ô]` when `a` is integral. For
an extension `L / K` of number fields, the algebra norm `New.adeleNorm` on finite adeles preserves
the module.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ideleAbs`: the module is multiplicative, and it is a continuous positive character
  (`New.continuous_ideleAbs`, `New.ideleAbs_pos`).
* `New.ideleAbs_toAdele`: the product formula for the diagonal embedding `New.toAdele`, for a
  totally complex `E`.
* `New.finIdeleAbs`: the module `∏ ‖x_w‖` of a finite idele; `New.finIdeleAbs_principalIdele` is the
  finite part of the product formula.
* `New.genIndex_eq_inv_finIdeleAbs`, `New.genIndex_eq_inv_norm`: for a finite idele, or an element
  of `E_wˣ`, the index `New.genIndex` is the inverse of its module.
* `New.map_mulVec_haar_finAdele`, `New.volume_map_mulVec_adele`, `New.volume_map_mul_mul_adele`:
  pushing Haar measure forward along `x ↦ a x` or `x ↦ a x b` divides it by the module of the
  determinant of that map.
* `New.finIdeleAbs_adeleNorm`: the norm keeps the module `New.finIdeleAbs` of a finite idele.

Notions from other files:
* `New.𝔸f E`, `New.Ô E`: the finite adeles of `E`, and the subring of those that are integral at
  every finite place.
* `New.FinPlace E`, `New.LocField w`: the finite places of `E` and the completion `E_w`; `w.q` is
  the order of the residue field at `w`, and `w.below K` is the place of a subfield `K` below `w`.
* `New.locIdele w x`: the finite idele with component `x` at `w` and `1` elsewhere.
* `New.idelesUnitOff S`: the finite ideles that are units at all places outside `S`.
* `New.genIndex a`: the inverse of the factor by which multiplication by a unit `a` scales Haar
  measure, and `0` for a non-unit.
modules.literature:
Known result: the module of an idele, the product formula and the scaling of Haar measure.

Part of a known result: functoriality of ideles under the norm map, restricted here to the module
and to supports.

modules.title: Idelic generators of ideals, semilocal fields and tame local characters
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adeles of number fields, characters and approximation
modules.note:
The file collects local and idelic facts about number fields. For a CM field `E` it computes values
of the splitting character `υ`, and with `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E` it shows that `New.Ô E` in the
finite adeles forms an adelic pair. It defines Schwartz–Bruhat functions, semilocal fields and tame
local characters, and shows that a finite product of completions is a semilocal field. An auxiliary
fact gives the valuation of natural numbers prime to one of valuation less than 1.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_reduction_and_idele_generator`: a nonzero ideal `I` of `𝓞 E` has an idelic generator
  `t` in the integral finite adeles `New.Ô`, and `Ô / t Ô = 𝓞 / I`.
* `New.upsilon_toAdele`: the splitting character `υ` (`New.SplittingChar`) is trivial on the
  principal ideles.
* `New.upsilon_eq_prod_mul_of_v_eq`, `New.upsilon_eq_atUniformizer_zpow`,
  `New.upsilon_atUniformizer_mul_star`: values of `υ`, which is unramified at all finite places,
  computed from the valuations of the finite part and the values at the chosen uniformisers.
* `New.schwartzBruhat`: locally constant, compactly supported complex functions that vanish outside
  a set. `New.schwartzBruhat.comp`, `New.schwartzBruhat.isLocallyConstant_curry` and
  `New.integral_mem_of_isLocallyConstant` are tools for substituting and averaging.
* `New.SemilocalField`: conditions on a topological ring `F` that a finite product of
  non-archimedean local fields meets, with ring of integers `O` and uniformiser `ϖ`.
* `New.invOnUnits`, `New.TameLocalChar`: `χ⁻¹` cut off to the units of `O`, and the data showing
  that it comes from a primitive character (`New.Exchange.IsPrimitiveMulChar`) of the finite ring
  `O / ϖ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsAdelic`: The properties of the pair Ô ⊂ 𝔸_f abstracted to R ⊂ A: R is open, compact and
  stable under conjugation, locally a valuation ring, contains a skew element i with −i·i = 1 and an
  element of trace 1, and −1 is a norm from R.
* `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040`: `E` contains a primitive root of unity of order `7! = 5040`.
* `New.SplittingChar`: a unitary Hecke character `υ` of `E` that complex conjugation inverts and
  whose value at an idele `x` with unit finite part is `∏ x_τ / |x_τ|` over the infinite places
  `τ`; `υ.atUniformizer w` is its value at the chosen uniformiser at the finite place `w`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.ClassField.Global.CMSplittingCharacters` and `Lib.Weil.TameGaussSum` for sources.

modules.title: Products of completions at finite sets of places and approximation of adeles by elements of E
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adeles of number fields, characters and approximation
modules.note:
Let `S` be a finite set of finite places of the number field `E`. The ring `New.LocProd S` is the
product of the completions `E_w` for `w ∈ S`, and `O` is the product of their rings of integers. The
file relates `New.LocProd S` to the finite adeles through the projection `New.evalPlaces S` and the
extension by zero `New.adeleOfLocal S`. It computes the projection of Haar measure and the
generalized index of an element of `New.LocProd S`, and it bounds the zeta function of `O`. For a CM
field `E` and `S` stable under conjugation it defines the involution of `New.LocProd S`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_principal_near_of_mem_differentIdeal`: approximation of an adele by an element of `E`.
* `New.integralOff`, `New.locProd_O_eq_map_evalPlaces`, `New.map_evalPlaces_restrict_volume`: the
  adeles integral off `S`, and the effect of the projection `New.evalPlaces S` on the integral
  adeles `New.Ô E` and on Haar measure.
* `New.idealZeta_locProd_le`, `New.genIndex_eq_inv_prod_norm`, `New.sqrt_genIndex_le_prod_norm`: the
  zeta function of `O` and the generalized index.

Notions from other files:
* `𝔸f E`, `New.Ô E`: the finite adeles of `E` and the subring of those integral at every place.
* `New.LocField w`, `New.LocInt w`: the completion `E_w` at the finite place `w` and its integers.
* `New.genIndex a`: the inverse of the factor by which the unit `a` scales Haar measure, and `0` if
  `a` is not a unit.
* `Φ w`: the chosen complex embedding of `E` at the infinite place `w`, given by
  `New.PlaceEmbedding E`, which is part of `New.CMType E`.
* `New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E`: the CM field `E` contains a primitive `5040`-th root of unity.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Adelic.Adeles.Basic` for sources.

modules.title: Automorphic forms on adelic unitary groups, the Petersson product and rapid decay
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Automorphic, cuspidal and algebraic forms
modules.note:
This file studies functions on the adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f of a hermitian space V over E
with signs s. Here Γ = `V.Γ` is its group of rational points, and `V.quotMeasure` is the measure for
integrals over Γ\G. The forms of type e (see `New.Space.IsForm` below) make up an inner product
space under the Petersson product and carry an action of G_f. The height `New.Space.height` is the
inverse of the first minimum `New.Space.firstMinimum`, cut off at `1`. Moderate growth and rapid
decay are measured against the height, and the rapidly decaying automorphic functions form a
subrepresentation. When Γ is cocompact, in particular when all signs of V are equal, every
automorphic function has rapid decay.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.IsAutomorphic`: continuous, left Γ-invariant functions with a level.
* `New.Space.IsForm`: bounded automorphic functions that are fixed by convolution with a kernel e if
  e is integrable (for e not integrable this condition is empty). A form is bounded and measurable
  (`IsBoundedMeasurable`, which follows from bounded and continuous), hence lies in L²(Γ\G).
* `New.Space.Form`: the space of these forms, an inner product space under the Petersson product
  `New.Space.petersson`, with the action `New.Space.formRep` of G_f.
* `New.Space.rapidFunctions`: the automorphic functions of rapid decay form a subrepresentation.
* `New.Space.isRapid_of_isCocompact`: continuous Γ-invariant functions are rapid when Γ is
  cocompact.
* `New.Space.IsAutomorphic.mem_rapidFunctions`: automorphic functions are rapid when all signs are
  equal.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Space.Γ`: for a space (J, x), the subgroup x^{-1} U(J)(E) x of G, the image of the rational
  unitary group.
* `New.GInf`: the archimedean unitary group G_∞ for signs s: one copy of the complex unitary group
  U(diag s) for each infinite place of E.
* `New.Space.IsModerate`, `New.Space.IsRapid`: |F| ≤ C·ht^B for some C and B; |F|·ht^B is bounded
  for every B.
modules.literature:
Known result: automorphic forms on unitary groups and their rapid decay. Cusp forms are treated in
`Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.Cuspidality`.

modules.title: Convolution over real points, cusp kernels, the Petersson product and Poincaré series
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Automorphic, cuspidal and algebraic forms
modules.note:
Let G = G_∞ × G_f be the adelic unitary group, and let R(α)F(g) = ∫ α(x) F(gx) dx over G_∞ be right
convolution over the real points (`New.realConv`). For integrable α, R(α) preserves bounded
automorphic functions, and convolving with an idempotent kernel e produces forms of type e. The
product of discrete series kernels over the infinite places is a cusp kernel under a gap condition.
For the Petersson product, right translation is unitary, and a cusp kernel e projects every real
translate of a form of type e to a multiple of it. A bounded Poincaré series, projected term by
term, is a form.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.continuous_realConv`, `New.Space.isAutomorphic_realConv`: for integrable α, R(α)F is
  continuous when F is bounded, measurable and has an open level, and it is automorphic and bounded
  when F is also invariant under the rational points.
* `New.Space.exists_form_eq_realConv`: convolving with an idempotent kernel gives a form of type e.
* `New.IsCuspKernel`: minimal idempotents e on G_∞ with a moment of order B + 1 and decay of order
  B, and with α ∗ e = e for some continuous compactly supported α.
* `New.isCuspKernel_typeKernel`: the product kernel `New.typeKernel` over the infinite places is
  such a kernel when the parameters satisfy a gap condition.
* `New.Space.IsForm.realConv_translate`, `New.Space.IsForm.petersson_real_translate`: `e` projects
  each real translate of a form to a multiple of the form.
* `New.Space.exists_form_eq_tsum_of_fixesLeft`: if an absolutely bounded sum of measurable functions
  is left invariant under `V.Γ` and has level `K`, projecting each term by R(e) gives a form of type
  `e`; `New.Space.exists_form_eq_tsum` is the case of a sum over `V.Γ` of translates of one
  function. `New.levelSpace (V.formRep e) K` is the space of forms of type `e` fixed by the open
  subgroup `K` of the finite points.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space.IsAutomorphic`: continuous, left invariant under the rational points `V.Γ`, and right
  invariant under some open subgroup of G_f.
* `New.HCParam.dsKernel`: for a parameter l = 2λ, the function e_λ on U(diag s), the formal degree
  times the conjugate of the discrete series coefficient c_λ (`New.HCParam.dsCoeff`).
* `New.IsIdempotentKernel` (part of `New.IsCuspKernel`): e is continuous and integrable, e(g⁻¹) is
  the conjugate of e(g), e(1) ≠ 0, and ∫ e(z)e(x⁻¹z⁻¹y) dz = e(x⁻¹)e(y)/e(1).
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Space.quotMeasure`: the measure on `G` that computes integrals over `Γ \ G`.
modules.literature:
Known result: convolution over real points, cusp kernels, the Petersson product and Poincaré series
projected to forms, from the theory of cusp forms. For sources see
`Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.Cuspidality`.

modules.title: The mean along a unipotent radical vanishes; reduction in the radical
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Automorphic, cuspidal and algebraic forms
modules.note:
This file defines the adelic unipotent radical `New.unipotentRadical` of the stabiliser of the
span of the columns of an isotropic adelic matrix. A bounded continuous function that is fixed by
right convolution with a cusp kernel `e` (`New.IsCuspKernel`) and invariant under the rational
points of the radical, of finite covolume, has mean zero along the radical. From this it derives a
bound by the oscillation for such functions. It also gives the matrix algebra for the reduction
step, `New.Reduction.radicalElem` and `New.Reduction.IsIntBounded`, which moves an adelic point of a
unipotent radical close to `1` by a rational element.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.integral_unipotentRadical_eq_zero`: the mean along the radical vanishes.
* `New.unipotentRadical`: the points `g` of the adelic unitary group that fix the span `A` of the
  columns of `a` pointwise and satisfy `uᴴ J (g v) = uᴴ J v` for all `u`, `v` in `A^⊥`, where
  `J = stdForm E s`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places (in the coordinates x⁻¹ X this
  form is the adelic matrix `stdForm E s`); `V.Γ` is its group of rational points in the adelic
  group G = G_∞ × G_f, and `V.move g` has the point xg.
* `New.realConv`: R(k)F(g) = ∫ k(x) F(gx) dx over G_∞ (`New.GInf`, one copy of U(diag s) for each
  infinite place of E), for k on G_∞ and F on G.
* `New.IsCuspKernel`: a minimal idempotent for convolution on G_∞ that decays polynomially and is
  reproduced by a compactly supported function.
* `New.dilationGroup a`: the pairs (g, c) such that g is the scalar c on the columns of a and
  wᴴ J (g v) = wᴴ J v for all v, w orthogonal to these columns.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.Cuspidality` for sources.

modules.title: Cuspidality bounds, unipotent reduction, rapid decay and finite dimension of forms
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Automorphic, cuspidal and algebraic forms
modules.note:
This file studies forms of type `e` (`New.Space.IsForm`) on the adelic unitary group of a hermitian
space `V`, for a cusp kernel `e` (`New.IsCuspKernel`). At a point with a short lattice vector,
short vectors span a cusp: a rational isotropic subspace whose radical is covered by its rational
points times a small real ball and a level. A bounded continuous function that is fixed by `e` and
invariant under the rational points of a unipotent radical, of finite covolume, has mean zero along
the radical (`New.Space.integral_unipotentRadical_eq_zero`, in
`Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.UnipotentRadical`). The rational points are cocompact in the radical
of a rational isotropic subspace, so forms are cuspidal. Forms then decay faster than every power
of the height, and those of a fixed level span a finite-dimensional space.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.exists_cuspFrame`: let `N ≠ 0` be a natural number in the different of `E`, `M ≠ 0` and
  `0 < δ ≤ 1`. If the first minimum is less than `(δ / (M κ²))ⁿ`, with `κ = New.cuspConst E n N`,
  short lattice vectors span a rational isotropic subspace `A ≠ 0` and its orthogonal
  (`New.Space.CuspFrame`), and `N_A` lies in `(Γ ∩ N_A) Z_δ J(M)` (`New.Space.RadicalCovered`),
  where `Z_δ` is the real ball of radius `δ` about `1` and `J(M)` is the principal level `M`.
* `New.Space.IsCuspidal`, `New.Space.IsForm.isCuspidal`: cuspidal functions; forms are cuspidal.
* `New.Space.IsCuspidal.norm_le_of_firstMinimum_lt`: at such a point `g`, a cuspidal function of
  level `M` is at most its oscillation under real right translations of size `δ`.
* `New.Space.exists_norm_mul_height_pow_le`, `New.Space.IsForm.mem_rapidFunctions`: forms decay
  faster than every power of the height, uniformly at a fixed level.
* `New.Space.finite_levelSpace`: the forms of a fixed level span a finite-dimensional space.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places (in the coordinates x⁻¹ X this
  form is the adelic matrix `stdForm E s`); `V.Γ` is its group of rational points in the adelic
  group G = G_∞ × G_f, and `V.move g` has the point xg.
* `New.realConv`, `New.Space.IsForm`: R(k)F(g) = ∫ k(x) F(gx) dx over G_∞ (`New.GInf`, one copy of
  U(diag s) for each infinite place of E), for k on G_∞ and F on G. For integrable e, a form of
  type e is a bounded automorphic function fixed by R(e). Here e is a cusp kernel
  (`New.IsCuspKernel`): a minimal idempotent for convolution on G_∞ that decays polynomially and
  is reproduced by a compactly supported function.
* `New.Space.height`: the height ht(g) = 1/λ, with λ the first minimum cut off at 1
  (`New.Space.firstMinimum`) of the moved space `V.move g`.
* `New.unipotentRadical` (in `Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.UnipotentRadical`): the adelic unipotent
  radical of the stabiliser of the span of the columns of an isotropic matrix.
* `New.Reduction.radicalElem` (in `Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.UnipotentRadical`): the matrix
  `1 + 2 (T - Tᴴ - Tᴴ J T) J`; for hermitian `J` and `T = w aᴴ` with `aᴴ J a = aᴴ J w = 0`, it
  preserves `J`, fixes `a` and acts trivially on `a^⊥ / a`.
modules.literature:
Known results: cusp forms decay rapidly, and those of a fixed type and level make up a space of
finite dimension. Here a form is a bounded function reproduced by an integrable minimal idempotent,
with no differential equation. Cuspidality is used as a bound by the oscillation along unipotent
orbits, with an explicit depth, and the cusp is spanned by the shortest vectors of a sorted
Minkowski basis.

Sources: A. Borel, Automorphic forms on reductive groups (Park City lectures), IAS/Park City Math.
Ser. 12 (2007) 7-39, sections 7.6-7.9 and 8.3-8.4; I. Satake, Caractérisation de l'espace des
Spitzenformen, Sém. H. Cartan 10 (1957/58), exp. 9 bis; R. Godement, Série de Poincaré et
Spitzenformen, ibid., exp. 10; R. Godement, The spectral
decomposition of cusp forms, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 9 (1966) 225-234; S. Miller and W. Schmid, On
the rapid decay of cuspidal automorphic forms, Adv. Math. 231 (2012), arXiv 1106.2149; G. Muić,
Smooth cuspidal automorphic forms and integrable discrete series, arXiv 1610.05483 (cuspidality
through N. Wallach, On the constant term of a square integrable automorphic form, 1984).

modules.title: Algebraic forms on definite unitary groups, their pairing and Harish-Chandra parameters
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Automorphic, cuspidal and algebraic forms
modules.note:
This file studies forms on the definite unitary group of a hermitian space. A weight `(κ, e)`
records, at each infinite place `τ`, the number `κ τ h` of columns of height `h` of a Young diagram
and the power `e τ` of the determinant.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.AlgForm`: functions `φ` on the finite adelic points `New.Gf` with `φ(γ g) = ρ(γ) φ(g)` for
  rational `γ`, where `ρ = New.Space.weightRep`, whose stabiliser under right translation is open;
  `New.algFormRep` is right translation.
* `New.algFormCoeff`, `New.ofAlgForm`: from a form `φ` to the function `(x, g) ↦ L (ρ(x⁻¹) φ(g))`,
  `ρ = New.conjWeylRep`, for any linear form `L` and for the pairing with `New.highestVector`.
* `New.smoothPairing`, `New.smoothPairing_formTranslation`: a pairing B of coefficient vectors
  invariant under `New.Space.weightRep` gives a pairing of forms, by integration over Γ\G_f,
  invariant under G_f.
* `New.IsHCParam.eq_hcParameter`, `New.IsHCParam.exists_decreasingPosition_eq`: the entries of a
  parameter `l` are those of `New.hcParameter`, in the decreasing order of `l`;
  `New.IsHCParam.lowestKType_eq`: the highest weight that `l` determines.
* `New.highestVector_cyclic`: for injective `l w` and signs all 1, the highest vector
  `New.highestVector` of `New.conjWeylRep` is cyclic (`New.span_translate_highestVector_eq_top`),
  and so is its dual (`New.span_gramForm_highestVector_comp_eq_top`).
* `New.IsHCParam.prod_formalDegree`: the product of the formal degrees `New.HCParam.formalDegree` is
  the dimension.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Space.embFin`: For a space (J, x), the homomorphism U(J)(E) → G_f sending γ to the finite
  part of x^{-1} γ x.
* `New.conjWeylRep`: The complex linear representation of weight (κ, e) of the product over places
  of the unitary groups of signs s, acting by the matrices `New.conjWeylMatrix`.
* `New.IsHCParam`: `l` lists twice the Harish-Chandra parameter of the weight `(κ, e)`, in some
  order: at each place `w` the numbers `l w i` are distinct, and each of them is
  `hcParameter κ e (card n) w p` for some position `p < card n`.
* `New.HCParam.dsCoeff`: The function c_λ(g) = Ξ(a, a⁻¹g) of a complex matrix g, with a the block
  diagonal part of g and Ξ the normalised integral `New.HCParam.flenstedJensen`.
modules.literature:
Known result: algebraic modular forms on definite unitary groups, their invariant pairing and
Harish-Chandra parameters. Source: B. Gross, Algebraic modular forms, Israel J. Math. 113 (1999).

modules.title: Automorphic forms on standard definite spaces as algebraic forms
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Automorphic, cuspidal and algebraic forms
modules.note:
On a standard definite space (`New.Space.IsStd`: all signs `1` and point `x = 1`), this file
identifies automorphic forms with smooth algebraic forms. Let `ρ = New.conjWeylRep κ e` be the
representation of the compact group `G_∞` of weight `(κ, e)`, `d` its dimension, and
`v⁺ = New.highestVector` its highest unit vector when `l` matches the weight. An algebraic form
`φ` (`New.AlgForm`, vector valued on `G_f`) gives `φ♮ = New.ofAlgForm l s φ` with
`φ♮ (x, g) = ⟨v⁺, ρ(x⁻¹) φ(g)⟩`. The inverse map sends a form `y` to
`y♭ g = d ∫ y(x, g) ρ(x) v⁺ dx`. This file also writes integrals over `Γ \ G` as class sums over
`Γ \ G_f`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.toAlgForm`: the two maps are inverse between forms of type `New.typeKernel l` (fixed by
  `realConv k y (x, g) = ∫ k(z) y(xz, g) dz` for `k = typeKernel l 1`, which is
  `z ↦ d ⟨v⁺, ρ(z) v⁺⟩`) and smooth algebraic forms, by Schur orthogonality, when `l` matches the
  weight (`New.IsHCParam`).
* `New.Space.toAlgForm_formRep`, `New.Space.algFormEquiv`, `New.hasHeckePolynomial_toAlgForm_iff`:
  the equivalence commutes with `G_f`, so it respects levels and Hecke eigenvalues.
* `New.Space.integral_eq_classIntegral_of_isLevel`,
  `New.Space.integral_mul_eq_classIntegral_toAlgFormFun`, `New.Space.integral_mul_eq_classIntegral`:
  integrals over `Γ \ G`, in particular against `φ♮`, as class sums `New.classIntegral` over
  `Γ \ G_f`.
* `New.Space.classSum_gramForm_eq_mul_petersson`: for two algebraic forms that transform under a
  level by one character with values of finite order, the class sum of their Gram pairings is a
  multiple of the Petersson product of the associated functions.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s), for the signs s, at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Space.IsAutomorphic`: a function on `G = G_∞ × G_f` that is continuous, left invariant under
  rational points and right invariant under an open subgroup of `G_f`.
* `New.algFormCoeff s L φ`: the function `(x, g) ↦ L (ρ(x⁻¹) φ(g))`; it is `New.ofAlgForm l s φ` for
  `L = ⟨v⁺, ·⟩`, where `⟨·, ·⟩ = New.gramForm`.
* `New.stdLevelIndex K`: the index `[stdLevel : K ∩ stdLevel]` in the standard level
  `stdLevel = New.stdLevel E n`; a level (`New.IsLevel K`) is an open subgroup `K ≤ stdLevel`.
* `New.classIntegral Γ K f`: the integral of `f` over `Γ \ G_f` for `vol K = 1`, as a finite sum; in
  this file `Γ = New.stdRatPoints`, the rational points of the standard space.

Known result: algebraic modular forms as functions on the adelic group. For the source see
`Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.SmoothAlgebraicForms`.

modules.title: Algebraic modular forms: delta forms, unitary translation and spanning by Hecke eigenforms
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Automorphic, cuspidal and algebraic forms
modules.note:
This file concerns algebraic modular forms. These are functions on a group that transform on the
left by a representation of a group `Γ` embedded in it, and on the right by a character of a level.
`New.levelSpace π K χ` is the space of vectors on which `K` acts through `χ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.deltaForm`: the form supported on one double coset, made from a vector. Its values are sums
  over the finite sets `New.transporter` (`New.deltaForm_apply`); `New.classSum_deltaForm` gives the
  class sum of its values under an invariant family of additive maps `W →+ ℂ`.
* `New.freeLevelEquiv`, `New.finrank_levelSpace_smoothFormRep`: at a sufficiently small level, also
  called free (all `New.classAut` trivial), forms are arbitrary families of values, so the dimension
  is the class number times `finrank ℂ W`.
* `New.Space.exists_isUnitary_formTranslation`: right translation `New.Space.formTranslation` on the
  forms `New.Space.forms` of weight `κ` has an invariant positive definite scalar product.
* `New.Space.finite_formTranslation_levelSpace`: the eigenforms of an open level for
  `New.Space.formTranslation` form a finite-dimensional space.
* `New.hasHeckePolyAt_iff`: a form has a Hecke polynomial at a split place exactly when it is
  spherical there and an eigenvector of the Hecke operators there, the polynomial being formed from
  the eigenvalues.
* `New.le_span_isSphericalOff`: a finite-dimensional Hecke-stable space of forms fixed by the
  integral points trivial at `S` is spanned by simultaneous eigenforms.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space E n ε`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over a field E with a CM
  structure (`CMType E`) and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx equal to diag(ε) at the infinite places and 1 at
  the finite places; the signs `ε = 1` give the definite spaces.
* `New.Space.forms`: Algebraic modular forms of weight κ on a definite space V: functions f on G_f
  with open right stabiliser and f(γg) = ρ_κ(γ)f(g) for rational γ, ρ_κ = `New.Space.weightRep` for
  a weight κ : `New.Weight E`; values lie in `WeylIndex n κ.1 → ℂ`.
* `New.HasFiniteType Γ K`: `K` is compact and open, `Γ \ G / K` is finite and every group
  `New.classAut Γ K g`, which is `Γ ∩ g K g⁻¹`, is finite.
* `New.classSum Γ K f`: the sum over the classes `c`, with representative `g_c`, of
  `f g_c / #(Γ ∩ g_c K g_c⁻¹)`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Finite dimension of spaces of algebraic modular forms and the Hecke eigenforms
spanning them. Related files: `Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.SmoothAlgebraicForms` and, for congruence
subgroups and level structures, `Lib.Adelic.Unitary.CongruenceLevels`.

modules.title: Periods of algebraic forms over a block subgroup as class sums via branching
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Automorphic, cuspidal and algebraic forms
modules.note:
This file takes an algebraic form `ψ` on a definite unitary group of rank `m + 1`, a finite point
`u` of rank one and an automorphic `Φ(x, g) = L_g(ρ₀(x) c)` on the block subgroup of rank `m`.
It turns the integral of `Φ(h) ψ_t(diag(h, u))` into a class sum (`New.classIntegral`) over the
finite adelic points. Here `ψ_t = New.algFormCoeff 1 t ψ`, and `ρ`, `ρ₀` are the representations
`New.conjWeylRep` of weights `(κ, e)` and `(κ₀, e₀)`. The archimedean integral gives an
intertwiner from weight `(κ, e)` to weight `(κ₀, e₀)`, which multiplicity one for branching
(`New.SpansBranchingMaps`) makes a multiple of the given matrix `A`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Seesaw.integral_algFormCoeff_blockEmb`: the period over a block subgroup as a class sum.
* `New.Seesaw.isAutomorphic_algFormCoeff_blockEmb`: for a finite point `u` of rank one, the
  restriction `h ↦ ψ_t(diag(h, u))` to a block is automorphic on the smaller standard space.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space.IsAutomorphic`: a function on `G = G_∞ × G_f` that is continuous, left invariant under
  rational points and right invariant under an open subgroup of `G_f`.
* `New.algFormCoeff s L φ`: the function `(x, g) ↦ L (ρ(x⁻¹) φ(g))`; it is `New.ofAlgForm l s φ` for
  `L = ⟨v⁺, ·⟩`, where `⟨·, ·⟩ = New.gramForm`.
* `New.classIntegral Γ K f`: the integral of `f` over `Γ \ G_f` for `vol K = 1`, as a finite sum.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.AutomorphicAsAlgebraic` for sources.

modules.title: The p-adic gauge of algebraic forms, class sums, and integral forms of a level
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Automorphic, cuspidal and algebraic forms
modules.note:
Fix a prime `p` and a map `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]`, written ι in prose and given by the instance
`[ι : PadicPlace p]`. The gauge `New.weylGauge κ e g ξ` is the largest `p`-adic absolute value of a
coordinate of `g⁻¹ ι(ξ)`, for a finite adelic unitary point `g` acting in weight `(κ, e)`. It
measures the `p`-integrality of the values of algebraic forms (`New.AlgForm`). The file proves
invariance properties of the gauge, bounds the forms `New.deltaForm` on `New.stdSpace E n` that are
supported on one double coset, bounds class sums over `Γ \ G / K`, and studies the sizes of
algebraic forms whose level is cut out at finitely many split places.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_mul_mem_integralAbove`: a rational point moves `g` to a point integral above `p`.
* `New.LevelPlaces.LevelForm`: forms of weight (κ, e) on which the level `New.levelOf` of H acts
  through χ, a finite-dimensional inner product space under the class sum of the Gram pairing.
* `New.gramForm_mem_embValRing`: the Gram pairing of two vectors of gauge at most one, for
  `ι ∘ conj` and for `ι`, is integral; `New.LevelPlaces.LevelForm.norm_nsmul_inner_le_one`: so is
  the inner product of two such forms, after multiplication by a common multiple of the orders of
  the stabilisers.
* `New.LevelPlaces.LevelForm.valueCoord`, `New.LevelPlaces.LevelForm.valueMetric`: coordinates of a
  form in which the inner product has a rational matrix, if the classes have no nontrivial
  automorphisms.
* `New.Rows.weylGauge_classSum_le_one`: `p`-integrality (gauge `New.weylGauge` at most one) passes
  to the class sum after multiplication by a common multiple of the orders of the stabilisers.

Notions from other files:
* `New.weylGauge`: at the infinite place τ, g⁻¹ acts through its component at the prime induced by
  the embedding x ↦ ι(Φ_τ(x̄)) of E into ℂ_p.
* `New.stdSpace`: the definite space `I_n`, the sum of `n` norms with its standard lattice.
* `New.integralAbove`: the subgroup of finite adelic unitary points whose components at all primes
  above p are integral invertible matrices.
* `New.classSum`: the class sum of f, that is, the sum over the double cosets c in Γ\G/K of
  f(g_c)/#(Γ ∩ g_c K g_c⁻¹), with g_c a chosen representative; `New.classAut` is Γ ∩ gKg⁻¹.
* `New.stdLevel`: K₀ = G_f ∩ GL_n(Ô), the stabiliser of the standard lattice in the finite adelic
  unitary group G_f = `New.Gf`; `New.maxCompactAt n w` is its part supported at w and w̄.

Known; see `Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.SmoothAlgebraicForms` and `Lib.Adelic.Hecke.ClassSums` for

modules.title: Level spaces, Hecke operators, stabilisers and class sums
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Hecke operators and class sums
modules.note:
For an abstract group `G` with subgroups `Γ`, `K`, `H` and a representation `π` over a commutative
semiring, this file defines the level space of `K`, Hecke operators and weighted class sums over
`Γ \ G / K`. The Hecke operator `New.heckeFun π K f = ∑ f(g) π(g)` sums over chosen representatives
`g` of `G ⧸ K` and is applied to vectors fixed by `K`. When `f (g * k) = f g` for `k ∈ K` and `v` is
such a vector, the term `f g • π g v` depends only on the coset `g K`. The file proves that, under
this condition, the value at `v` does not depend on the choice of representatives.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.levelSpace`: the vectors on which `K` acts through a character `χ`.
* `New.heckeFun`, `New.heckeCoset`: the operator `∑ f(g) π(g)` over chosen representatives of
  `G / K`, and its value on the indicator function of a double coset `K g K`.
* `New.classAut`, `New.classSum`: the stabiliser `Γ ∩ g K g⁻¹`, and the sum over `Γ \ G / K`
  weighted by the inverse orders of the stabilisers.
* `New.relIndex_mul_measure_inf`, `New.measure_inter_eq_inv_relIndex`: for `K` compact and `H` open,
  the volume of `H ∩ K` times the index `[K : H ∩ K]` is the volume of `K`.
* `New.heckeFun_eq_sum`, `New.heckeFun_eq_sum_pullback`: on a vector fixed by `K`, the sum over any
  other system of representatives.
* `New.heckeFun_heckeFun`: on a vector fixed by `K`, the composite of two operators is the operator
  of a convolution.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Adelic.Hecke.ClassSums` for sources.

modules.title: Class sums as integrals over Γ\G, orbit unfolding and means over compact subgroups
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Hecke operators and class sums
modules.note:
For subgroups `Γ`, `K` of a topological group `G`, `New.classSum Γ K f` is the sum of
`f g / #(Γ ∩ g K g⁻¹)` over representatives `g` of `Γ \ G / K`, where
`Γ ∩ g K g⁻¹ = New.classAut Γ K g`. The integral over `Γ \ G` with `vol K = 1` is defined from class
sums as the finite sum `New.classIntegral`, also called the mean (it is an average when `Γ = ⊥` and
`K` is the whole group). No measure theory is used. The mean `New.classIntegral` is used to average
smooth representations over compact subgroups.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.classIntegral`: the class sum at the level `rightStabilizer f ⊓ K`, divided by its index in
  `K`.
* `New.HasFiniteType`: finitely many classes and finite stabilisers, with `K` open and compact.
* `New.classSum_eq_relIndex_smul`: change of level, by double counting.
* `New.classIntegral_eq_classSum_mul`, `New.classIntegral_eq_inv_smul_classSum`: for left
  Γ-invariant f, the mean can be computed at a smaller open level that fixes f, or one whose
  conjugate by some a lies in K and fixes f (then for the right translate of f by a).
* `New.classIntegral_sum`: for smooth left Γ-invariant functions, the mean commutes with finite
  sums, additive maps and right translation.
* `New.compactMean ρ H`: the mean over H. It is invariant under H on both sides
  (`New.apply_compactMean`, `New.compactMean_apply`), projects onto the H-fixed vectors
  (`New.compactMean_mem_levelSpace`, `New.compactMean_eq_self`), and is self-adjoint for an
  invariant scalar product (`New.IsUnitary.compactMean_adjoint`).

Notions from other files:
* `Subgroup.FixesLeft`: `Γ.FixesLeft f` says that `f (γ * g) = f g` for all γ in Γ and g in G.
* `New.levelSpace π K χ`: For a representation π of G, a subgroup K and a character χ of K (by
  default trivial), the submodule of vectors v with π(k)v = χ(k)v for all k in K.
modules.literature:
Known result: weighted class sums for a pair (G,K), as in the theory of abstract Hecke operators and
of algebraic modular forms. They make sense for values in any rational vector space, without a Haar
measure. Source: G. Shimura, Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions
(1971), ch. 3; B. Gross, Algebraic modular forms, Israel J. Math. 113 (1999) 61-93; M. Greenberg and
J. Voight, Lattice methods for algebraic modular forms on classical groups, arXiv 1209.2460.

modules.title: Quotient measures via cutoffs: unfolding, covolume, unimodularity, periodic means
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Measures on quotients and unfolding
modules.note:
A group `H` with a measure `ν` acts on a measure space `(X, μ)`. Integration over `H \ X` is done on
`X` itself. A cutoff (`New.IsCutoff ν β`) is a measurable `β : X → [0, ∞]` with
`∫ β (h • x) dν(h) = 1` for every `x`. For a discrete subgroup `Γ` of a group `G` with counting
measure, and a Haar measure `μ` on `G`, `Γ.quotMeasure μ` integrates over `Γ \ G`, and its total
mass is the covolume of `Γ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.orbitMeasure`: the measure `β μ` on `X`, for the chosen weight `β = New.chosenCutoff ν`. It
  is meant for `H`-invariant integrands, and for actions where a cutoff exists (`New.HasCutoff`);
  then `β` is a cutoff (`New.isCutoff_chosenCutoff`).
* `New.IsCutoff.measurePreserving`, `New.measurePreserving_orbitMeasure`: the map `(x, h) ↦ h • x`
  carries `(β μ) × ν` to `μ`; the other results on unfolding follow from this and Fubini's theorem.
* `New.identDistrib_orbitMeasure_of_unfold`, `New.identDistrib_orbitMeasure`: invariant functions
  have the same distribution for every measure that unfolds to `μ`. So the choice of cutoff does not
  matter when `ν` is inversion invariant and `μ` is invariant, both s-finite.
* `New.integral_quotMeasure_tsum`: `∫_{Γ\G} ∑_γ f(γ g) = ∫_G f`.
* `New.isMulRightInvariant_of_finite_covolume`: a group with a discrete subgroup of finite covolume
  is unimodular.
* `New.quotMean_tsum_eq_integral`: the mean of `x ↦ ∑ γ, F (γ + x)` is `∫ F dμ` divided by the
  covolume.
modules.literature:
Known result: Invariant integration on a quotient (Weil's formula), unfolding and unimodularity.
Here the quotient integral is integration against a measurable weight of total mass one on each
orbit, so no orbit space or section is needed to define it; existence is proved for proper actions
and for discrete subgroups. Source: O. Kallenberg, Invariant measures and disintegrations with
applications to Palm and related kernels, Probab. Theory Related Fields 139 (2007) 285-310 (as
cited in D. Gentner, G. Last, Math. Z. 267 (2011), §2); for the classical form, N. Bourbaki,
Intégration VII, 1963.

modules.title: Unfolding over orbits and integration in Iwasawa coordinates
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Measures on quotients and unfolding
modules.note:
This file proves integration formulas on a quotient `Γ \ G` by a discrete subgroup `Γ`. An integral
over `Γ \ G` of a sum over translates is unfolded to an integral over the quotient by the subgroup
that keeps a block, in particular by the stabiliser of a point. Integrals of functions invariant
under a closed subgroup `N` are then written in Iwasawa coordinates `G = N · i(M) · K`.

* `Γ.quotMeasure μ`: the measure on `G` that integrates left `Γ`-invariant functions over `Γ \ G`.
* `N.FixesLeft F`: `F (γ * g) = F g` for all `γ ∈ N` and `g ∈ G`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.integral_tsum_eq_integral_tsum_block`: the integral over `Γ \ G` of the sum over all
  translates of a block `C` is the integral over `S \ G` of the sum over `C`, where `S` is the
  group that keeps `C`. `New.integral_tsum_block` adds integrability and termwise integration.
* `New.integral_tsum_orbit_eq_integral_stabilizer`: the case of one orbit, with `S` the image of the
  stabiliser of a point.
* `New.lintegral_iwasawa`: `dn dm dk` in the coordinates `i m * n * k` is a multiple of Haar
  measure.
* `New.integral_quotMeasure_iwasawa`: the integral over `Γ \ G` of a function `F` invariant under
  `N` and `Γ` is a nonzero constant times the integral of `w m * F (i m * k)`, where conjugation by
  `i m` scales the Haar measure of `N` by `w m`.
modules.literature:
Known result: The unfolding trick and the integration formula in Iwasawa coordinates on a quotient
by a discrete subgroup. Weil's formula for invariant integration on a quotient is in
`Lib.Adelic.QuotientMeasure.Basic`.

modules.title: Moving a quotient from one variable to another
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Measures on quotients and unfolding
modules.note:
Let `Λ → R` be a homomorphism from a countable group to a subgroup `R` of a group `G`, and let `F`
on `R × G` be invariant under the diagonal action of `Λ`. The integral of `F` over
`Λ \ (R × G)` may be computed as an integral over `R × (Λ \ G)` or over `(Λ \ R) × G`
(`New.integral_cutoff_swap`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.orbitMeasure ν μ`: the measure `μ` weighted by a chosen cutoff; it computes integrals over
  the quotient.
modules.literature:
A consequence of a known result: the integral over a quotient does not depend on the cutoff. See
`Lib.Adelic.QuotientMeasure.Basic`.

modules.title: Pushing forward quotient measures, unfolding in stages and vanishing criteria
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Measures on quotients and unfolding
modules.note:
This file studies integrals over a quotient `Γ \ G` by a discrete subgroup `Γ`, with `μ` a Haar
measure. For a `Γ`-invariant `F`, `(Γ.quotMeasure μ)[F]` is the integral of `F` over `Γ \ G`. Such
integrals are compared with integrals over a quotient `Λ \ H` of a second group mapping to `G`, and
are written as iterated integrals with inner integral over `Λ \ H`. From this follow two criteria
for the integral of a continuous left `Γ`-invariant function to vanish.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_integral_comp_quotMeasure_eq_smul`: for a continuous surjection `H → G` of unimodular
  groups taking `Λ` into `Γ`, the integral over `Λ \ H` of a pulled-back invariant function is a
  fixed multiple of its integral over `Γ \ G`. Unimodular means the Haar measures are also right
  invariant.
* `New.integral_quotMeasure_stages`: the integral over `Γ \ G` is an iterated integral whose inner
  integral is over `Λ \ H`.
* `New.integral_quotMeasure_eq_integral_cosetMeasure`: the case of a closed subgroup, with the outer
  integral over `i(H) \ G` (`New.cosetMeasure`).
* `New.Exchange.exists_integral_stages_eq_mul`: for a subgroup `L × H`, if the inner integrals
  through every `g` are `ρ g * c`, with `re ρ` nonnegative and nonzero near some point, then the
  integral over `Γ \ G` is `R * c` for a fixed `R ≠ 0`, with `Γ` the image of `Λ ≤ H`.
* `New.integral_quotMeasure_eq_zero_of_mean`: the integral vanishes if an average of translates of
  `F` by elements of a closed subgroup `H ≥ Γ` is `a • F` and these elements scale the Haar measure
  of `H` by `d ≠ a`.
* `New.integral_quotMeasure_eq_zero_of_twist`: the integral vanishes if `F (u * y) = c • F y` with
  `‖c‖ = 1` and `c ≠ 1`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Adelic.QuotientMeasure.Basic` for sources.

modules.title: Transference, first minima and short bases of lattices of hermitian spaces
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Reduction theory for adelic unitary groups
modules.note:
Minkowski's bound and weak transference in a Euclidean space `E` of dimension `m` give short vectors
and a covering radius for a subgroup `Λ` whose dual has no nonzero vectors shorter than `ρ > 0`. For
a hermitian space `V` with a point, the lattice of `V` defines a first minimum, cut off at `1`, and
a height on the adelic unitary group, against which growth and decay are measured.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.weak_transference`: if `m ≥ 1`, `Λ` has a nonzero vector shorter than `2 m / ρ`.
* `New.weak_transference_covering_radius`: every vector is within `m ^ 2 / ρ` of `Λ`.
* `New.Space.archCoords`, `New.Space.firstMinimum`, `New.Space.height`: the archimedean coordinates
  of a rational vector, the first minimum of the lattice cut off at `1`, and the inverse of the
  first minimum of the moved space `V.move g`, the height at `g`.
* `New.Space.IsModerate`, `New.Space.IsRapid`: moderate growth and rapid decay against the height.
* `New.Space.form_eq_zero_of_norm_mul_lt_one`, `New.Space.firstMinimum_move_eq_one`,
  `New.Space.firstMinimum_pos`: lattice vectors whose lengths have product below `1` are orthogonal;
  the minimum is `1` in a definite space, and positive in any space as the lattice is discrete. The
  comparison of heights on `Γ g Ξ` for compact `Ξ` is `New.Space.exists_height_le_mul` in
  `Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.Basic`.
* `New.Space.exists_short_basis`: the lattice contains a basis of vectors of length at most a
  constant over the first minimum.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over a CM field E (class
  `CMType E`) and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite
  places; `V.move g` is (J, xg).
* `New.G`: the adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f for signs s at the infinite places and the
  identity matrix at the finite places.
* `New.Space.vecAtPoint`: for a space (J, x), the adelic coordinates x⁻¹y of a vector y in E^n.
* `New.Space.baseLattice`: for a space (J, x), the lattice E^n ∩ x_f Ô^n, as an additive subgroup of
  E^n.
* `New.Space.sum`: for spaces V, W with signs s, t, the space with concatenated signs whose matrix
  and point are the block diagonal sums of those of V and W.
modules.literature:
Known result: Transference theorem for the covering radius of a lattice against its dual's first
minimum. The constant here is m squared in dimension m, where the sharp forms have a constant linear
in m. The result holds for any subgroup of a Euclidean space whose dual has no short nonzero vector,
and is proved by projecting along a short vector. Source: Lagarias-Lenstra-Schnorr, Korkin-Zolotarev
bases and successive minima of a lattice and its reciprocal lattice, Combinatorica 10 (1990); sharp
forms in Banaszczyk, Math. Ann. 296 (1993), and Miller-Stephens-Davidowitz, Kissing numbers and
transference theorems from generalized tail bounds, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 33 (2019).

See also `Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.Cuspidality` and `Lib.Adelic.Reduction.FiniteVolume`.

modules.title: Adelic Minkowski theorems and counts of rational points in boxes
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Reduction theory for adelic unitary groups
modules.note:
This file proves Minkowski's first theorem and the upper bound in his second theorem over the
adeles, for the lattice attached to `y : GL n (𝔸 E)`. This lattice consists of the rational vectors
`ξ` with `y⁻¹ ξ` integral at the finite places, measured by `y⁻¹ ξ` at the infinite places. Here
`New.𝔸 E` is `ℂ ^ f × 𝔸f E` with `f = New.Core.numInfPlaces E`; here `[CMType E]` makes `E` a number
field whose infinite places are all complex, each place `w` with a chosen embedding `Φ w : E → ℂ`.
`New.toAdele` is the diagonal embedding, `New.ideleAbs` the adelic absolute value and `New.Ô` the
ring of integral finite adeles, and the unit box is `ball 0 1 ×ˢ Ô E` (sup norm) in each coordinate.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.minkowski_first`: a lower bound for the number of rational `ξ` with `y⁻¹ ξ` in the unit box.
* `New.Core.twoAtInfinity`, `New.Core.dyadicDiag`, `New.Core.profileBases`: the idele that is `2` at
  infinity, the diagonal matrices `D` of its powers, and the rational bases `Y` with `y⁻¹ Y D⁻¹` in
  a given set.
* `New.Core.frameLattice`, `New.Core.frameLength`: the lattice of `y` and the Euclidean length of
  `y⁻¹ ξ` at infinity.
* `New.Core.minkowski_second_theorem`: the second theorem. The lattice contains a basis of `E ^ n`
  for which `|det y|` times the product of the `2 f`-th powers of the lengths is bounded in terms of
  `f`, `n` and the discriminant. The proof takes successive minima and applies the first theorem to
  a box without nonzero lattice vectors.
* `New.exists_basis_frameLength_le_two_zpow`: a bound of the same kind, with a larger constant, for
  the lengths rounded up to powers `2 ^ x j`.
* `New.Core.encard_le_of_dyadic_box`: at most `C * 4 ^ (f * ∑ i, (x i)⁺)` rational vectors `ξ` have
  the vector of the `twoAtInfinity E ^ (-x i) * ξ i` in a given compact set.
* `New.Core.exists_eq_zero_of_zpow_mul_mem`: for a compact set `B` of adeles and all large `m`, no
  nonzero `a` in `E` has `twoAtInfinity E ^ m * a` in `B`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ratVectors`: the image of `E ^ n` in `𝔸 E ^ n` under the diagonal embedding, as an additive
  subgroup.
modules.literature:
Part of a known result: Reduction theory, here the adelic Minkowski theorems. For Mahler-Godement
compactness and finite covolume see `Lib.Adelic.Reduction.FiniteVolume`.

modules.title: Adelic reduction theory, Mahler's criterion and finite volume of the arithmetic quotient
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Reduction theory for adelic unitary groups
modules.note:
This file develops reduction theory for `GL_n` over the adeles: every adelic frame `y` has a
rational basis `Y` such that `y⁻¹ Y` lies in one fixed compact set after its columns are scaled by
powers of `2` at the infinite places. For a hermitian space `V` (`New.Space`), a weighted Haar
measure on the adelic unitary group `G` computes integrals over `[G] = V.Γ \ G`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Core.exists_isCompact_profileBases`: one compact set `M` bounds a reduced basis at every `y`.
* `New.exists_isBoundedDualBasis`: Mahler's criterion for frames of forms that may vary. The
  criterion for the unitary group of one space is `New.Space.mahler_criterion` in
  `Lib.Adelic.Reduction.DefiniteClassSums`.
* `New.Space.quotMeasure`: for a space `V` with rational points `New.Space.Γ`, the measure
  `Subgroup.quotMeasure` on `G` for counting measure on `Γ`. It integrates `Γ`-invariant functions
  over `[G] = Γ \ G`.
* `New.Space.lintegral_encard_ne_top`: the count of rational `n × t` matrices is integrable over
  `V.Γ \ G` if `2 t < n`.
* `New.Space.isFiniteMeasure_quotMeasure`: finite volume, the case `t = 0`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.𝔸`: the ring `ℂ ^ f × 𝔸_f`, one copy of `ℂ` for each infinite place of `E` times the finite
  adeles. It is the adele ring of `E` when `E` is totally complex; `New.toAdele` embeds `E` in it.
* `New.ideleAbs`: the module (adelic absolute value) of an idele.
* `New.Core.twoAtInfinity`: the idele of `E` that is `2` at all infinite places and `1` at the
  finite places.
* `New.Core.profileBases M x y`: the `Y` in `GL_n(E)` with `y⁻¹ Y (D x)⁻¹ ∈ M`, where
  `D x = New.Core.dyadicDiag x` is diagonal with entries `twoAtInfinity E ^ x i`. The integer vector
  `x` is called the profile of such a basis.
* `New.Space`: a matrix `J` over `E` and a point `x` in `GL_n(𝔸)` with `xᴴ J x` equal to `diag s` at
  the infinite places, for signs `s`, and `1` at the finite places.
modules.literature:
Known results: reduction theory for adele groups (the compactness criterion of Mahler and Godement,
finite covolume) and Weil's convergence criterion. Finite volume is proved here only for unitary
groups over CM fields, by counting reduced bases, and Weil's criterion only when twice the number of
vectors is below the rank. The adelic Minkowski theorems come from
`Lib.Adelic.Reduction.MinkowskiTheorems`, with crude explicit constants. Source: A. Borel, Some
finiteness properties of adele groups over number fields, Publ. IHES 16 (1963), 4.5-5.8; A. Weil,
Sur la formule de Siegel dans la théorie des groupes classiques, Acta Math. 113 (1965), Prop. 8;
Bombieri-Vaaler, On Siegel's lemma, Invent. Math. 73 (1983).

For the adelic points of unitary groups and their Haar measures, see
`Lib.Adelic.Unitary.WeakApproximation`.

modules.title: Mahler's criterion for hermitian spaces and class sums for definite spaces
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Reduction theory for adelic unitary groups
modules.note:
For a hermitian space `V : New.Space E n s`, the rational unitary group embeds in the adelic unitary
group `New.G E s` with image `V.Γ`, and in its finite part with image `V.Γf`. Mahler's criterion
follows from short bases, whose Gram matrices take finitely many values. It gives compactness modulo
the rational points when all signs agree. For the signs `1`, it also gives finiteness of classes.
For such a space, the integral over `Γ \ G` of a suitable invariant function is then a class
sum. Here `K₀` is `New.stdLevel`, and `New.classSum` sums over the double cosets `Γf \ G_f / K` with
weights `1 / #(Γf ∩ g K g⁻¹)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.mahler_criterion`: Mahler's criterion; the `g` of bounded height lie in `V.Γ * C` for
  one compact set `C`.
* `New.Space.isCocompact_of_definite`: if all signs agree, the adelic group is compact modulo
  `V.Γ`. `New.Space.isCocompact_Gamma` is the case of the signs `1`.
* `New.Space.isCocompact_finitePart`: for the signs `1`, the finite part of the group is
  compact modulo `V.Γf`.
* `New.Space.hasFiniteType_of_isLevel`: for the signs `1`, finitely many classes with finite
  stabilisers.
* `New.Space.integral_quotMeasure_eq_classSum`: take a space with signs `1` and a continuous, left
  `Γ`-invariant function on `G`. Suppose that its average over the infinite places is fixed under
  right translation by an open `K ≤ K₀`. Then its integral over `Γ \ G` is `[K₀ : K]⁻¹` times the
  class sum of this average. `New.Space.classIntegral_eq_integral` is the case of functions of the
  finite part.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s), with s the signs, at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Space.move`: the space `V.move g` is the space with the same J and the point x g; its lattice
  `baseLattice` is the lattice at `g`, and the norm of `archCoords u` is the length of u at `g`.
* `New.Space.height`: the height ht(g) = 1/λ, with λ the first minimum cut off at 1
  (`New.Space.firstMinimum`) of the moved space `V.move g`.
* `New.IsLevel`: an open subgroup of `K₀`, with index `New.stdLevelIndex` in `K₀`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Adelic.Reduction.FiniteVolume` and `Lib.Adelic.QuotientMeasure.Basic` for sources.

modules.title: Traces on the range of an idempotent from traces of a raising operator
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Let `T⁺`, `T⁻` be adjoint operators on a finite-dimensional inner product space with
`T⁺ * T⁻ = d • (1 + c • e)`, where `d, c > 0`, `e` is idempotent and `A` commutes with `T⁺` and
`T⁻`. The traces of the `A ^ l * T⁺ ^ i`, `l, i ≥ 1`, determine the trace of `A` on the range of `e`
(`LineRelation.trace_mul_mean_eq`): on the generalised eigenspace of `A` for each non-zero
eigenvalue they give the eigenvalues of `T⁺`, hence the dimension and
`|det T⁺| ^ 2 = d ^ dim * (1 + c) ^ rank e`.

The first section collects what traces determine on generalised eigenspaces; in particular the
traces of all powers of an operator determine its characteristic polynomial
(`charpoly_eq_of_trace_pow_eq`).

modules.title: The elements of a group algebra that keep a level
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
For a representation `ρ` of a group `G` and a subgroup `K`, the elements of the group algebra
`ℂ[G]` that map `K`-fixed vectors to `K`-fixed vectors form an algebra, and it acts on the
`K`-fixed vectors.

Notions from other files:

* `levelSpace ρ K`: the subspace of the vectors that `ρ k` fixes for every `k ∈ K`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the elements of a group algebra that keep the vectors fixed by a subgroup, and their
action on these vectors. The related class sums are in `Lib.Adelic.Hecke.ClassSums`.

modules.title: Lines and hyperplanes over a field
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
This file describes the stabilisers in `GL_n` of the line of a basis vector `e_i` and of the
complementary coordinate hyperplane. Over a finite field it counts the linear forms with value `1`
at `e_i`, and those with value `1` both at `e_i` and at a vector off its line. It shows that `0`
is a simple root of the characteristic polynomial of a matrix of block shape `(0 ∗; 0 g')`
with `g'` invertible.

Notions from other files:
* `parabolic lev`: the subgroup of `GL_n` of the matrices `g` with `g a b = 0` whenever
  `lev b < lev a`. The two stabilisers use level functions with values in `Prop`, ordered by
  implication.
modules.literature: Standard linear algebra.

modules.title: Test functions and the two local conditions of the comparison of traces
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Test functions on a topological group, their translates, and the function `a ⋆ 1_K` of an element
`a` of the group algebra. On the finite adelic group the comparison of traces asks for two
conditions: the test function is cuspidal at a split place (`IsCuspidalAt`), and at a second place
the components of the elements of its support are integral with a simple eigenvalue zero modulo the
place. `HasSimpleZero` is this last property of one matrix over the completion at the place.

Notions from other files:
* `Gf E n`: the group of finite adelic points of the unitary group of the `n × n` identity matrix;
* `LocField w`, `LocInt w`, `ResField w`, `localIntGL n w`: the completion at a finite place `w`,
  its ring of integers, its residue field, and `GL_n` of that ring inside `GL_n` of the completion;
* `ofSplitPlace hw`: at a split place `w`, the map from `GL_n` of the completion at `w` to `Gf E n`;
* `radicalHom`: for an idempotent `ε`, the homomorphism `Y ↦ 1 + ε Y (1 - ε)` onto the unipotent
  radical of the parabolic subgroup that keeps the image of `ε`.
modules.literature: Known; see `Lib.Adelic.TraceFormula.TraceComparison` for sources.

modules.title: An irreducible label in a tuple gives a cuspidal test function
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Green's class function of a monic irreducible polynomial is cuspidal: over a finite field, it has
mean zero on the unipotent radical of every proper parabolic subgroup of `GL_n` that is cut out by
coordinates. If the polynomial is a label of degree `n` (so its constant term is nonzero), it
follows that the coefficients of its idempotent have sum zero over each coset of such a radical.
Inflated to the finite adelic group, the idempotent of a tuple of polynomials, one of which is an
irreducible label, gives a test function that is cuspidal at the place of that member.

Notions from other files:
* `labelChar θ c` is the class function of Green that belongs to the polynomial `c` and the
  multiplicative character `θ`, here always the chosen `faithfulChar k`; `labelIdem n c`
  is its idempotent in the group algebra of `GL_n`, and `tupleIdem n c` the tensor product of these.
* `radicalHom` at the projector `p` on a set `T` of coordinates sends `Z` to the element
  `1 + p Z (1-p)` of the unipotent radical of the parabolic subgroup of `T`. Sums over the radical
  are taken over all matrices `Z`, so that every element is counted equally often.
* `levelOf w ⊥` is the kernel of the reduction `stdLevel.reduceFamily w` of `stdLevel E n`, the
  maximal compact subgroup of the finite adelic unitary group `Gf E n`, at the places `w i`;
  `liftResidue` is a section of that reduction.
* `convIndicator _ _ a` is the convolution of `a` with the indicator of an open compact subgroup,
  and `IsCuspidalAt _ φ` says that all translates of `φ` have sum zero over the cosets of the proper
  radicals at a split place.
modules.literature:
The finite-field input is part of Green's theory of the characters of `GL_n(F_q)`; see
`Lib.LocalGL.Green.TauFunctions`.

modules.title: Integration over the fibres of a conjugation map
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
A group `Γ` acts on a group `G` by conjugation through `j : Γ → G`. Let `X` be a slice of a closed
set `C ⊆ G` (`IsSlice`): the map `(g, y) ↦ g y g⁻¹` from `Γ × X` onto `C` is open in the sense of
`IsSlice.eventually_exists_conj_mem`, and its fibres are the orbits of a closed subgroup `H` of `Γ`.
The file proves two steps of the descent of invariant distributions from `C` to `X`.

* Step 1, images. Integration over the fibres takes a test function `Ψ` on `Γ × G` to a test
  function on `C`. A test function on `G` that extends it is an image of `Ψ` (`IsImage`), and one
  exists (`IsSlice.exists_isImage`).
* Step 2, Haar measure. An invariant distribution on `C` kills the image of `Ψ` as soon as the
  integrals of `Ψ (·, y)` over `Γ` vanish for all `y ∈ X`
  (`IsInvariantDistribution.eq_zero_of_isImage`).

Functions on `Γ × X` and on `C` are handled as restrictions of test functions on `Γ × G` and on `G`.

Notions from other files:
* `TestFunction G`: the locally constant functions of compact support from `G` to `ℂ`.
* `TestFunction.translate (a, b) f`: the test function `x ↦ f (a⁻¹ * x * b)`.
* `compactMean ρ L x`: the mean of the orbit of the vector `x` under a compact subgroup `L`.
modules.literature: Known result: descent of invariant distributions to a slice, after Harish-Chandra.

modules.title: The stabiliser of an isotropic subspace
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Let `J` be a nondegenerate hermitian form and `A` an isotropic subspace, spanned by the columns of
a matrix `X`. An isometry that keeps `A ≠ 0` has a reducible characteristic polynomial. If an
isometry keeps `A`, its characteristic polynomial does not change under left multiplication by the
unipotent radical of the stabiliser of `A`.

Notions from other files:
* `U J` is the unitary group of `J`: the invertible matrices `g` with `gᴴ * J * g = J`.
* `dilationGroup X` consists of the pairs `(g, c)` of an isometry and a unit such that
  `g * X = c • X` and `g` is the identity on `A^⊥` modulo its radical. Its members with `c = 1`
  form the unipotent radical.

modules.title: The stabiliser of a line at a finite place
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Let `w` be a finite place of the number field `E`, with local field `LocField w` (the `E_w` of
`GL_n(E_w)`), valuation `v`, ring of integers `𝒪`, uniformiser `ϖ` and residue field of `q`
elements. In the formulas, `n` also stands for the cardinality of the index type `n`, and the
exponent `n - 2` is an integer. Let `J_line ⊂ GL_n(𝒪)` be the stabiliser of the line of a basis
vector `e_i` modulo `w`. We write `diag (ϖ, 1, …, 1)` for the diagonal matrix with `ϖ` at the index
`i` and `1` elsewhere. Let `T⁺`, `T⁻` be the operators of the double cosets of this matrix and of
its inverse, and let `e_sph` be the mean over chosen lifts to `GL_n(𝒪)` of the elements of `GL_n` of
the residue field, which on vectors fixed by the kernel of the reduction modulo `w` is the mean over

modules.title: Coprime factors
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Let `w` be a split place, `A, B` coprime non-units of `E_w[X]`, and `C` the set of elements of the
finite adelic group `Gf E n` with characteristic polynomial `A B` at `w`. An invariant distribution
`I` on `C` kills every test function `φ` that is cuspidal at `w` (`eq_zero_of_coprime_factors`).

Let `H` be the block diagonal subgroup of `GL_n(E_w)` with blocks of sizes `deg A` and `deg B`, `N`
the group of the unipotent matrices `1 + z` with `z` an upper right block, and `X ⊆ C` the set of
the `y` whose component `y_w` is block diagonal, with `A, B` as characteristic polynomials of the
blocks up to scalars. First `φ` is replaced by the mean of its conjugates under `GL_n(O_w)`.

* Step 1, images. The projection onto the kernel of `A(y_w)` along the kernel of `B(y_w)` is a fixed
  polynomial in `y_w` for `y ∈ C`. So `X` is a slice of `C` for `H` (`isSlice_blockLocus`), and test
  functions `Ψ` on `GL_n(E_w) × X` can be integrated over the fibres of `(g, y) ↦ g y g⁻¹`.
* Step 2. If the integrals of `Ψ (·, y)` vanish, then `I` kills the image of `Ψ`. This is
  `IsInvariantDistribution.eq_zero_of_isImage`, proved for any slice.
* Step 3, the choice of `Ψ`. Put `Ψ (g, y) = φ (g y g⁻¹)` for `g` in `U = GL_n(O_w) N` and `0`
  otherwise. This is the restriction to `GL_n(E_w) × X` of a test function on `GL_n(E_w) × Gf E n`
  (`exists_testFunction_eq_indicator`), its image is `φ` times the volume of `H ∩ GL_n(O_w)`
  (`isImage_blockLocus_smul`), and its integrals over `GL_n(E_w)` vanish because the conjugates of
  `y ∈ X` under `N` fill the coset `y N` (`integral_indicator_iwasawaSet_eq_zero`).

* `upperBlocks ε` is the set of the upper right blocks, the matrices `z` with `ε z = z` and
  `z ε = 0`.

  idempotent `ε`; `coordProjector T` is the projector on the coordinates in `T`.
* `intGL n O` is `GL_n(O)`, and `localIntGL n w` is `GL_n(O_w)`. A `TestFunction` on a space is a
  locally constant function to `ℂ` with compact support; `φ.1` is the function itself.
* `IsSlice j H C X`, for a continuous homomorphism `j` of `Γ` into a group, says that
  `(g, y) ↦ j g * y * (j g)⁻¹` takes `Γ × X` onto the closed set `C`, has local sections, and has
  the orbits of `H` as fibres; `IsImage j ν X Ψ f` says that `f` is the integral of `Ψ` over the
  fibres.
