modules.title: Convergence of the geometric side
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Let `k` be a function on the real points that decays against a high power of the norm, and let `φ`
be a test function on the finite points. The sums of `(k ⊗ φ)(x⁻¹ γ x)` over rational points `γ`
converge absolutely, with a bound by a power of the height of `x`. High in a cusp, short lattice
vectors span an isotropic subspace `A`, and the bound improves: for the `γ` that move `A`, the
points `x⁻¹ γ x` are large at infinity, and, if `k` is a cusp kernel, the terms of the `γ` that keep
`A` cancel along the unipotent radical. So the sum over the `γ` whose characteristic polynomial lies
in a given set is bounded uniformly in `x` and in the set, and the sum over the `γ` with irreducible
polynomial is bounded absolutely. These are known arguments for convergence in a simple trace
formula (cf. Flicker and Kazhdan).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space E n s`: a hermitian form `J` over `E` with an adelic point. `G E s` is the unitary
  group `GInf E s × Gf E n`, and `V.ratEmbed` embeds the rational unitary group `U V.J` in it.
* `New.Space.height`: `V.height x` is the inverse of the first minimum, cut off at `1`, of the space
  `V.move x` whose point is moved by `x`.
* `New.IsCuspKernel B k`: `k` is a minimal idempotent kernel on the real points with decay of order
  `B`, an integrable moment and a compactly supported function that reproduces it.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.exists_tsum_enorm_kernelTerm_le_height`: the bound by a power of the height.
* `New.Space.exists_norm_tsum_polyTerm_le`: the uniform bound for a set of polynomials.
* `New.Space.exists_tsum_enorm_irreducibleTerm_le`: the absolute bound for irreducible polynomials.

modules.note:
This file shows that the conjugate of the kernel of a level `K` is a form of type `e`. It expands
the kernel of `e ⊗ (a ⋆ 1_K)` in an orthonormal basis of forms. It writes `vol K` times the trace
on forms as the integral over `[G] = Γ \ G` of the kernel on the diagonal. It introduces classes
of pairs (finite frame, rational matrix) and orbital integrals, and it unfolds the term of an
irreducible characteristic polynomial into orbital integrals. It ends with triple kernels, the
rotation of triples and the trace property of this rotation.

  the kernel of a level `K` is a form, and the kernel of `e ⊗ (a ⋆ 1_K)`, for `a` in the group
  algebra of `G_f`, expands in an orthonormal basis.

  over `Γ \ G` of the kernel on the diagonal.
* `New.frameClass`, `New.Space.orbitalIntegral_unfold`: classes of pairs (finite frame, rational

modules.title: Comparison of traces of operators on forms for different spaces and signs
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Trace formula for unitary groups of hermitian spaces
modules.note:
A simple trace formula for the unitary group of a hermitian space `V`, with terms sorted by the
characteristic polynomials `R` of rational points. The test function is `e ⊗ φ`, with `e` a cusp
kernel on the real group and `φ` locally constant of compact support on the finite adelic group.

This file proves the Selberg principle: orbital integrals of an irreducible `R` with a root off
the unit circle vanish. For `R` with all roots on the unit circle, it splits orbital integrals into
real and finite factors and matches the classes of different signs. It concludes that the trace on
forms depends neither on the space nor on its signs.

* `New.Space.orbitalIntegral_eq_zero`: the orbital integral is `0` if `R` is irreducible with a root
  off the unit circle.
* `New.Space.exists_geometricSide_singleton_eq`: if `R` is irreducible with all roots on the unit
  circle, `E` contains the 5040th roots of unity and has an even number of infinite places, and the
  parameter has a large gap, its term is a product of characters of the compact unitary group times
  a number that depends only on `R` and `φ`.
* `New.trace_comparison`: let `E` contain the 5040th roots of unity and have an even number of
  infinite places, let `n ≥ 2`, and let the parameter have a large gap. If `φ` is cuspidal at a
  split place and, at a place `w'`, the elements of its support are integral with `0` a simple root
  of the characteristic polynomial modulo `w'`, the reducible `R` contribute nothing, so the trace
  depends neither on the space nor on its signs.

Comparison of simple trace formulas for unitary groups that differ only at real places. Here
integrable idempotent kernels of very regular discrete series replace pseudo-coefficients, and the
CM field contains the 5040th roots of unity and has an even number of infinite places. There is no
truncation and no endoscopy. Source: Labesse, Changement de base CM et séries discrètes (2011),
Thms 5.4, 5.5 and their proofs; Arthur and Clozel (1989), ch. 1, Lemmas 2.4-2.6; integrable test
functions as in Knightly and Li, Traces of Hecke operators (2006); for the simple trace formula
with a cuspidal component, Flicker and Kazhdan (1988) and Harris and Labesse (2004), Prop. 1.10.5.

Selberg principle that orbital integrals of an idempotent vanish off the elliptic set. Here the
idempotent is a minimal convolution idempotent with polynomial decay on a product of groups
U(p,q), placed inside the adelic orbital integral of a rational point with irreducible
characteristic polynomial. If some eigenvalue has absolute value other than 1, this integral is
zero. Source: Harish-Chandra, Discrete series II, Acta Math. 116 (1966), Thm 11; Blanc and
Brylinski, Cyclic homology and the Selberg principle, J. Funct. Anal. 109 (1992); Hochs and Wang,
Orbital integrals and K-theory classes (2019), Cor 4.8.

modules.title: Adelic unitary groups over a CM field: levels, hermitian spaces, lattices and mass
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adelic unitary groups and hermitian spaces
modules.note:
This file defines unitary groups over the adeles of a CM field `E`, with signs `s` at the infinite
places. `New.Gf` is the finite adelic unitary group of the identity form, `New.stdLevel` is its
integral subgroup K_0, and `New.G` is the product G_∞ × G_f. A level is an open subgroup of K_0.
Given a CM type of `E` (`CMType E`, which fixes a complex embedding at each infinite place), a
hermitian space with a point is a form J over E together with an adelic matrix x such that xᴴJx is
diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite ones; it yields a rational subgroup and a
lattice. The mass is defined for the standard space, where J = 1 and x = 1.

Notions from earlier files:
* `𝔸 E`, `𝔸f E`: the adeles of `E` and its finite adeles; `Ô E`: the integral finite adeles;
  `toAdele : E →+* 𝔸 E` is the embedding of E in its adeles.
* `LocField w`, `LocInt w`: the completion E_w at a finite place w and its ring of integers;
  `evalAt w` takes a finite adele to its component at w.
* `U J`: the group of invertible matrices g with gᴴJg = J.
* `intGL n O`: the matrices in GL_n(R) that, with their inverses, have entries in the subring O;
  `congruenceGL M e`: those of them whose rows e(i) are congruent to rows of 1 modulo M.
* `star w`: the complex conjugate of a finite place w; w is split (`IsSplit`) if `star w ≠ w`.
  `star` on finite adeles is complex conjugation, and `conjLoc h : E_u →+* E_w` is the map it
  induces when `star u = w`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Gf`: the finite adelic unitary group G_f.
* `New.G`: the adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f.
* `New.mass`: the mass of the genus of O_E^l.

modules.title: Components of unitary adelic points at places; sums and moves of hermitian spaces
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adelic unitary groups and hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Elements of the finite adelic unitary group `New.Gf` of a CM field are studied through their
components `g.atPlace w`. The component at `w̄` is determined by the one at `w`, and is `1` exactly
when that one is, so supports have the form `S ∪ S̄`. Elements are cut along the idempotent
`New.idem` of a set of places. A hermitian space with a point `New.Space E n s` is a matrix `J` over
`E` together with `x` in `GL n (𝔸 E)` such that `xᴴ J x` is the diagonal matrix of the signs `s` at
infinity and `1` at the finite places.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Gf.componentOn`: keeps the components at `S ∪ S̄` and replaces the others by `1`.
* `New.Gf.exists_supportedOn_mul_trivialOn`: splitting into a part supported on `S ∪ S̄` and one
  trivial there.
* `New.Gf.mem_of_stdLevel_le_of_supportedOn_le`: `New.stdLevel` and the elements supported at one
  pair `w, w̄` generate the group.
* `New.range_ofSplitPlace`, `New.ofSplitPlaces`: elements with prescribed components at split
  places.
* `New.U.sum`, `New.G.sum`, `New.Space.sum`: block diagonal sums.
* `New.G.neg`, `New.Space.neg`: passing from signs `s` to `-s` (and from `J` to `-J`).
* `New.signedSpace`: the standard space with matrix `diag(s)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.idem`: The finite adele with component 1 at the places of a set and 0 elsewhere.
* `New.ofSplitPlace`: For a split place w, the homomorphism GL_n(E_w) → G_f sending g to the unitary
  element with component g at w and 1 off w, w̄.
* `New.G`: The adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f (an element `g` has adelic matrix `g.adeleMatrix`)
  for signs s at the infinite places and the identity matrix at the finite places.
* `New.stdForm`: The diagonal adelic matrix that is diag(s) at infinity and 1 at the finite places.

modules.title: Principal levels and levels defined by reductions in the finite adelic unitary group
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adelic unitary groups and hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Let G_f = `New.Gf` be the finite adelic unitary group of the CM field E. Let Ô = `New.Ô` be the
integral finite adeles of E. Let K₀ = `New.stdLevel` be the elements of G_f lying in GL_n(Ô). This
file studies open subgroups (levels) of K₀ of two kinds. The first is the principal level of a
nonzero integer a of E. It consists of the g in K₀ with all entries of g - 1 in aÔ. The second is
the level `New.levelOf w H` of the elements whose reductions at a family of places w_i lie in a
subgroup H. If the places are finitely many, distinct, and none is conjugate to any w_j, then
reduction is onto the product. For a character χ of H, the vectors on which this level acts through
reduction and χ carry an action of the groups that normalise H and fix χ.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_congruenceGL_subset`: every neighbourhood of `1` in `GL n` of the finite adeles
  contains a principal congruence subgroup of integer level. Here `New.Ô` is the ring of integral
  finite adeles, and `New.congruenceGL I id` is the group of matrices in `GL n` of it that are `1`
  modulo `I`.
* `New.principalLevel`, `New.isOpen_principalLevel`: the principal level of an integer a, open for
  a ≠ 0.
* `New.levelOf`: the k in K₀ whose reductions at a family of places w_i lie in a subgroup H of ∏
  GL_n(k_{w_i}); it is open for a finite family (`New.isOpen_levelOf`).
* `New.exists_reduceFamily_eq`, `New.relIndex_levelOf`: if the w_i are finitely many, distinct, and
  none is conjugate to a w_j, reduction is onto the product and the level has index [∏ GL_n : H].
* `New.relIndex_principalLevel_le`: the index of the principal level of `a ≠ 0` is at most
  `N(a) ^ (n ^ 2)`, where `N(a)` is the norm of `a`.
* `New.levelRep`: a group that normalises `H` and fixes `χ` acts on the vectors on which the level
  `New.levelOf w H` acts through reduction and `χ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Gf.atPlace`, `New.stdLevel.reduceAt`: The component at w of an element of G_f, and the
  reduction modulo w of an element of K₀. Elements of `trivialOn n P` have component 1 at each place
  in P.
* `New.ResField`: The residue field of the completion E_w of E at the finite place w.
* `New.levelSpace`: The vectors v with π(k)v = χ(k)v for all k in the level.
modules.literature:
Known result: Congruence subgroups and level structures of adelic groups. Here levels are preimages
of subgroups of the reductions at a family of places, or principal levels of a global modulus, in
the unitary group of the identity form. Source: V. Platonov, A. Rapinchuk, Algebraic groups and
number theory, ch. 3 and 5; B. H. Gross, Algebraic modular forms, Israel J. Math. 113 (1999) 61-93.

modules.title: The Gram matrix of a space is invertible and hermitian; group elements from isometries
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adelic unitary groups and hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Let `E` be a number field and `s : n → ℤˣ` a family of signs. The standard form `New.stdForm E s`
is its own inverse. It is hermitian when `E` has a CM type (`CMType E`), and then the Gram matrix
of a space is invertible and hermitian. For a CM field, matrices that preserve the standard form
give elements of the adelic unitary group.

## Notation

* `New.𝔸 E`: the adeles of `E`, with the diagonal embedding `New.toAdele : E →+* 𝔸 E`, given at
  the infinite places by the chosen CM type of `E`.
* `New.stdForm E s`: the diagonal adelic matrix with the signs `s` at the infinite places and `1`
  at the finite places.
* `New.Space E n s`: a matrix `J` over `E` with an invertible adelic matrix `x` such that
  `xᴴ * J.map toAdele * x` is `New.stdForm E s`.
* `New.G E s`: the adelic unitary group of the standard form; `New.G.adeleMatrix` is the matrix of
  an element.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.isUnit_J`, `New.Space.isHermitian_J`: `J` is invertible and hermitian.
* `New.G.ofMatrix`: the group element given by a matrix that preserves the standard form.

modules.title: Closed matrix embedding of adelic unitary groups, discrete rational points, weak approximation
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adelic unitary groups and hermitian spaces
modules.note:
This file concerns the adelic unitary group `New.G E s = G_∞ × G_f` over a CM field `E` (hypothesis
`IsCMField E`; the discreteness instance and the `New.Space` results assume `CMType E` instead,
which makes `E` a CM field), together with the rational points of a hermitian space `V` with signs
`s`. When all signs are `1`, the finite parts of the rational points form a discrete subgroup of
`G_f`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.G.isClosedEmbedding_adeleMatrix`: sending `g` to its adelic matrix is a closed embedding.
  Hence a map into the group is continuous when its matrix is (`New.G.continuous_iff`), and elements
  with the same matrix are equal (`New.G.ext_adeleMatrix`).
* An instance: for a space `W` whose signs are all `1`, the group `New.Space.Γf` of finite parts of
  the rational points is discrete in `G_f`.
* `New.Space.cayleyMap`: a map from all rational matrices to the rational points, through the Cayley
  transform of a rational skew matrix.
* `New.Space.eventually_tendsto_cayleyMap`: for all but finitely many parameters `c`, the image of
  `A` under this map tends to `g` at a given place as `A + e • B` (`A` rational, `B` adelic) tends
  to `V.toRatCoords g`, if the place kills the adeles `e` and `star e`.
* `New.Space.weak_approximation`: weak approximation. The consequence that a rational translate of a
  finite adelic point is integral above a prime is `New.exists_mul_mem_integralAbove`, in
  `Lib.Adelic.AutomorphicForms.PAdicGauge`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.G E s`: the adelic unitary group for the signs `s`; `New.G.adeleMatrix g` is the `n × n`
  matrix over the adeles of its element `g`.
* `New.Space E n s`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix `J` over `E` and `x` in
  `GL_n(𝔸)` with `xᴴ J x` equal to `diag s` at the infinite places and `1` at the finite places.
* `New.Space.ratEmbed`, `New.Space.embFin`: `γ ↦ x⁻¹ γ x` from the rational unitary group of `J` to
  `G`, and its finite part; their images are `New.Space.Γ` and `New.Space.Γf`.
* `New.Space.toRatCoords`: `g ↦ x g x⁻¹` from `G` to the adelic unitary group of `J`.
modules.literature:
Known result: weak approximation for unitary groups. Source: V. Platonov, A. Rapinchuk, Algebraic
Groups and Number Theory, 1994, ch. 7. Here a hermitian space comes with an adelic frame to a fixed
diagonal form, and this form is the identity at all finite places, so every space of one signature
shares one adelic group.

modules.title: Rational points and vectors of spaces under sums, moves and block embeddings
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Adelic unitary groups and hermitian spaces
modules.note:
Elementary facts on adelic unitary groups and hermitian spaces.

* `New.U.mem_range_sum_left`, `New.U.mem_range_sum_right`: which unitary matrices for a block
  diagonal form come from one block.
* `New.Space.mem_Gamma_iff_range`: `g` is a rational point iff `x g x⁻¹` has rational entries.
* `New.Space.witt`: Witt's theorem for the form of a space.
* `New.Space.stdForm_vecAtPoint`: in the coordinates of the point, the form `J` becomes
  `New.stdForm`.

A space `V` (`New.Space`) is a rational matrix `J` with an adelic point `x` such that `xᴴ J x` is
the standard form of signs `s`; `New.G E s` is the adelic unitary group of that form. Rational
unitary matrices and rational vectors are read in these coordinates by `V.ratEmbed γ = x⁻¹ γ x`,
with image `V.Γ`, and `V.vecAtPoint y = x⁻¹ y`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.G`: The adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f for signs s at the infinite places and the
  identity matrix at the finite places; `g.adeleMatrix` is the adelic matrix of `g`.
* `New.Space.sum`, `New.Space.reindex`, `New.Space.move`: the block diagonal sum of two spaces, the
  relabelling of the indices, and the space `(J, x a)` for `a` in G.
* `New.signedSpace`: the standard space with matrix diag(s), defined when E has a primitive 5040th
  root of unity (`New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040`).
modules.literature:
Witt's extension theorem for hermitian forms is classical; `New.Space.witt` is its matrix form
`New.witt` applied to the matrix of a space.

modules.title: Witt's theorem over fields and over Ô; quasi-reflections, Eichler maps, frames
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Witt's theorem, Eichler maps and Iwasawa decomposition
modules.note:
`J` is a hermitian matrix over a commutative ring with involution, with form
`h(u, v) = star u ⬝ᵥ J *ᵥ v`, and `New.U J` is the group of invertible `g` with `gᴴ * J * g = J`.
For invertible such `J`, Witt's theorem says that left invertible matrices with equal Gram matrices
differ by an element of `New.U J`. It is proved over a field with nontrivial involution using
quasi-reflections. Let `E` be a CM field that contains a primitive root of unity of order 5040
(`New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E`). Over its integral finite adeles `New.Ô E`, invertible hermitian
matrices have orthonormal bases, units fixed by conjugation are norms, and Witt's theorem is proved
for the standard hermitian form and primitive matrices, with an integral unitary matrix. For the
split form `T.splitGram` with `ϱ` hyperbolic planes and middle block `T`, the file then studies the
frame `f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` (`𝔰.besselFrame`, whose last entry `𝔰.besselFrame 𝔰.top` is `z`) and the
action of the unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU` on it.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.quasiReflection`: the quasi-reflection along `v`, for a unit `σ` with `σ + star σ = h(v, v)`.
* `New.witt_of_quasiReflection_mem`: left invertible `X`, `Y` with the same Gram matrix satisfy
  `g * X = Y` for some `g` in any subgroup of `New.U J` that contains all quasi-reflections.
* `New.witt`: the same with `g` in `New.U J`.
* `New.exists_orthonormal_Ô`: a hermitian matrix invertible over `Ô` is `Ô`-congruent to `1`.
* `New.witt_Ô`: Witt's theorem for primitive `n × k` matrices over `Ô`.
* `New.exists_unitary_eq_eichlerMap`: for hermitian `J`, the Eichler map
  `v ↦ v + h(u, v) x - h(x, v) (u + ς x)` (`New.eichlerMap`) is an isometry if `x` is isotropic, `u`
  is orthogonal to `x` and `ς + star ς = h(u, u)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape`: the data `𝔰` of a number `ϱ` of hyperbolic planes and a finite index set `κ`. A
  `T : 𝔰.Form A` is a square matrix indexed by `κ` and one more index `z`.
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: the Gram matrix of ϱ hyperbolic planes and a middle space with Gram
  matrix T: identity blocks pair the first and last ϱ indices, T is the middle block, all else is
  zero. Its unitary group is `T.G`.
* `New.Shape.Form.frameGram`: the (ϱ+1) × (ϱ+1) matrix of the products h(f_j, γ f_l) of the frame f
  with its image under γ, where h is the form `New.Shape.Form.splitGram T`.
* `New.frameMatrix`: the submatrix of γ on the rows and columns of the frame.
* `New.intGL`: for a subring O of R, the subgroup GL_n(O) of GL_n(R): matrices with entries in O
  whose inverse has entries in O.
modules.literature:
Known; see `Lib.Adelic.Witt.IwasawaDecomposition`, `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.FloorGroups` and
`Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.ComplexPlace` for sources.

modules.title: Smooth families of isometries that carry an isotropic vector to its neighbours
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Witt's theorem, Eichler maps and Iwasawa decomposition
modules.note:
Let `x₀` and `y₀` be isotropic vectors of a hermitian space over `ℂ` that are not orthogonal.
Elements of the unitary group that depend smoothly on `x` carry `y₀` to `x` for isotropic `x` near
`x₀` (they are built as quasi-reflections). For a form given by signs, each such element, composed
with the inverse of the one at `x₀`, carries `x₀` itself to `x`.

The notions used in the statements:
* `U J` is the unitary group of a matrix `J`: the invertible `g` with `gᴴ * J * g = J`.
* `signMatrix ε` is the diagonal matrix of the signs `ε i`, and `USign ε = U (signMatrix ε)`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Witt's extension theorem for hermitian forms, here in a smooth local form for
isotropic vectors. See also `Lib.Adelic.Witt.IwasawaDecomposition`.

modules.title: Maximal compact subgroup, splittings of isotropic frames and the Iwasawa decomposition
modules.folder: Adelic: Adeles, unitary groups and automorphic forms
modules.group: Witt's theorem, Eichler maps and Iwasawa decomposition
modules.note:
The file concerns the adelic unitary group `New.G E s` of a CM field `E` and its maximal compact
subgroup `New.maxCompact E s`, and the stabiliser of the span of k for a splitting of a hermitian
space along dual isotropic frames k, l. After the first section `E` carries a CM type and, for the
most part, Weil data (`New.WeilData`: roots of unity of order 5040, a purely imaginary element `j`
and further choices).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.exists_splitting`: every isotropic frame `k` of a hermitian space `V` is part of a
  splitting `V = range l ⊕ V₀ ⊕ range k` (`New.Space.Splitting`, a Witt decomposition). The proof
  compares `V` with the sum of a hyperbolic space and a standard space by Landherr's theorem
  (`New.Space.landherr`) and moves the frame by Witt's theorem (`New.Space.witt`).
* `New.Space.Splitting.radicalCentre`: the centre of the radical, parametrised additively by adelic
  matrices M through M − M*; it sends rational matrices to rational points.
* `New.Space.Splitting.centreCoeff`: the Fourier coefficients of a function along this centre.
* `New.Space.Splitting.iwasawa`: the Iwasawa decomposition for the maximal compact subgroup
  `New.maxCompact`, obtained at each infinite place and over the finite adeles from Witt's theorem
  (`New.Space.Splitting.iwasawa_of_witt`). The compact factor can be taken trivial where the given
  element is (`New.Space.Splitting.exists_mem_maxCompact_actsOnFrame_and_eq_one`).
* `New.Space.Splitting.exists_eq_radicalElement_mul_levi_mul_isAdapted`: every element is a product
  of an element of the radical, a Levi element and an element adapted to the splitting.

Notions from other files:
* `New.G E s`: the adelic unitary group of the form ε (`New.stdForm`) that is diag(s) at the
  infinite places and the identity at the finite places; `g.adeleMatrix` is the adelic matrix of
  `g`.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with
  xᴴJx = ε; `W.Γ` is the group of rational points in `New.G E s`.
* `New.U A`: the unitary group of a matrix A.
* `New.parabolic`: the invertible matrices that are block upper triangular for a level function.
modules.literature:
Known results: Witt's extension theorem for hermitian forms and for unimodular hermitian lattices,
and the Iwasawa decomposition. Witt's theorem is imported: over fields with a nontrivial involution
for invertible hermitian forms (`New.witt`), and over the integral finite adeles only for primitive
frames of the identity form over a CM field containing the roots of unity of order 5040
(`New.witt_Ô`). Its form in the maximal compact subgroup at an infinite place is deduced here: an
isotropic subspace is the graph of an isometry between the coordinates of the two signs. Source: U.
A. First, Witt's extension theorem for quadratic spaces over semiperfect rings, J. Pure Appl.
Algebra 219 (2015), Cor. 4.9 (for fields, Dieudonné, La géométrie des groupes classiques, 1955; for
lattices, Jacobowitz, Amer. J. Math. 84 (1962)). For the Iwasawa decomposition at the finite places:
J. Tits, Reductive groups over local fields, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 33 (1979), part 1, 3.3.2 and
3.8.1.
